Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision at the
intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by my first name for now, if that's okay. It's a long day already.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving and which direction you were headed when the collision
happened?
A: I was heading east through the intersection on a green light. I had been in the left lane and was going maybe
thirty-five miles an hour, give or take.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. It came from my right side, from the cross street. I saw a flash of white out of the corner of my eye and
then my car got hit on the passenger side. I hit the brakes but there wasn't time.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, always. The airbag on my side went off, so the belt was doing its job.
Q: Did you feel any injuries right after the collision?
A: My neck snapped to the side and I had a dull ache right away. By that evening it was stiff and I had trouble turning
my head to check my mirrors. I went to urgent care the next morning and they diagnosed a neck strain. They gave me
a muscle relaxer and told me to use ice and rest.
Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms?
A: Some days are better than others. Sitting at a desk for long periods makes it worse, and I can't really sleep on my
left side anymore.
Q: Did you speak with anyone at the scene about how the collision happened?
A: I told the other driver I didn't see them coming, and I gave the officer the same account. That's about all I
remember saying.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Just that I'm trying to keep up with my physical therapy appointments, and I want my car repaired properly so I can
get back to normal.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
